To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The traditional RTS/CTS mechanism does not work properly in 802.11n/ac WLANs due to the newly defined frame aggregation techniques in MAC layer.
the performance of 802. 11ac DCF in OBSS with hidden nodes is significantly degraded due to the increased number of hidden nodes.

(1) RTS/CTS handshake is not efficient enough to prevent the hidden terminal problem, (2) the performance of IEEE 80211ac DCF is better than that of IEEE 802 11n DCF, (3) the performance of DCF in 802.11 ac is better than that in 802 11 n in terms of throughput and packet loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance analysis of 11ac DCF in presence of hidden node and the effectiveness of DCF when using different primary channel and different bandwidth.
the performance of IEEE 80211ac WLAN with hidden nodes in OBSS environment and the effectiveness of RTS/CTS in 802.11 WLAN.
the performance analysis of 11ac DCF in presence of hidden terminals in OBSS environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 802.11n and 802.11a/b/g DCF mechanisms could be adopted to 802.11 ac DCF, but the RTS/CTS handshake needs to be modified to support the new 802.11 AC amendment.
the 802.11n and 802.11g DCF mechanism is still applicable in 802.11 ac WLANs.
IEEE 802. 11ac standard is a step forward in the evolution of WLAN, however, it is not a perfect one and there is still room for improvement in some aspects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of DCF in the 802.11 ac amendment is not satisfactory and needs further improvements.
the 802.11n DCF can be used in 802.11 ac WLAN without any significant performance degradation.
the 802.11n DCF is not sufficient for 802.11 ac WLAN and needs to be revised in order to support 802.11AC standard.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RTS/CTS handshake can not guarantee the elimination of collisions in OBSS environment, and it should be used only when the hidden nodes exist in the same BSS.
, when the channel width increases to 160 MHz and 80 MHz, the performance of the 802.11n and 802.11a DCF in OBSS environment is degraded.
the 802.11 DCF protocol needs to be modified to support the new 802.11 ac amendment.
